key_insight: PanoLOG makes panoramic 3D reconstruction practical by rethinking how large outdoor scenes are partitioned. Instead of relying on camera frustums that break under 360° ERP images, it uses geometry- and gradient-aware splitting to enable efficient coarse-to-fine optimization.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the high cost of reconstructing large outdoor scenes with 3D Gaussian Splatting, especially when using panoramic equirectangular images whose full-field visibility causes traditional block partitioning to fail and collapse into global training.
method: Proposes PanoLOG, a two-stage coarse-to-fine framework for panoramic outdoor reconstruction.
Introduces geometry-based and gradient-based partitioning to create effective local blocks despite omnidirectional visibility.
Enables block-wise optimization to remain localized and scalable rather than degenerating into full-scene training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more scalable way to reconstruct large outdoor environments from panoramic data with lower capture effort and reduced computation. It is especially useful for applications like mapping, virtual tourism, robotics, and urban digital twins.

paper_title: Geometry and Gradient-based Partitioning for Panoramic Outdoor Reconstruction
paper_authors: Weijian Chen, Weibo Yao, Yuhang Zhang, Xiaolin Tang, Guo Wang
